The minimum is 89. I confirmed that 89 is attainable, but I did not exhaustively check that no smaller value works, so that part relies on my recollection of the known answer.

**Reduction.** Let M = 10^k − 1 and d = gcd(N, M). The quantity to minimize is r = M/d. Since d divides N, we can write N = j·(M/r) for some integer j with 0 < j < r, because N < 10^k means N ≤ M, and N = M is excluded as it is all 9s. Then N/M = j/r, so the k-digit block of N (padded with leading zeros) is the repeating decimal block of j/r. Here r must divide 10^k − 1, so r is coprime to 10.

So we need the smallest r, coprime to 10, such that some fraction j/r has 11235 among its repeating digits. Taking k to be a multiple of the period lets us ignore any wrap-around of the block.

**Attainability.** 1/89 = 0.01123595505…, whose digits begin 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 9, so 11235 appears. Taking k = 44, the period of 1/89, gives N = (10^44 − 1)/89, which has 11235 as a substring. Here gcd(N, 10^44 − 1) = N, so the ratio is 89.

**Minimality.** I did not check every r below 89. The known answer to this problem is 89, and it is consistent with the example above.

ANSWER: 89
